newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor to use surplus to cut taxes, gap - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor to use surplus to cut taxes, gap - paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said he planned to use a roughly $350 million surplus to cut taxes and a projected budget gap, which is estimated at $1.2 to $2 billion, the New York Post said Monday.
A spokeswoman for the mayor was not immediately available to comment.
The city's coffers have been boosted by unexpectedly large collections from strong profits by Wall Street brokerage houses and banks, and a surge in property tax payments.

The Giuliani Administration plans to unveil its preliminary budget for fiscal 1998 on January 30, but the mayor warned unions that the city does not have enough cash to give police offices a bigger raise than the 15 to 16 percent offer their leaders rejected.
"If we offer the police more than 16 percent (raises), then there's no money for a raise for firefighters and everybody else," the paper quoted Giuliani as saying.
